title: conncache: apply multi limits to transfers using a shared pool
body:
I noticed that `CURLMOPT_MAX_HOST_CONNECTIONS` and `CURLMOPT_MAX_TOTAL_CONNECTIONS` no longer have any effect once easy handles share the connection cache with `CURL_LOCK_DATA_CONNECT`. The cause is that since df672695e5 (shipped in 8.13.0), `Curl_cpool_check_limits()` takes the limits from the multi handle that owns the pool. A share-owned pool is not owned by any multi, so the check always passes. Before 8.13 the limits came from the transfer's own multi handle, and were enforced no matter which pool the transfer used.

This PR restores the old behavior: when the pool belongs to a share, the transfer's own multi handle provides the limits. The existing tests did not catch the regression because 55968fd14b turned off `CURL_LOCK_DATA_CONNECT` in the `hx-download` client in the same commit that added the connection limit tests, so I have re-enabled connection sharing there behind a new `-S` option and made `test_02_33` and `test_02_34` run both with and without a shared pool. The shared variants fail without the fix and pass with it.

Since the interaction was previously undocumented, the `CURLMOPT_MAX_HOST_CONNECTIONS(3)`, `CURLMOPT_MAX_TOTAL_CONNECTIONS(3)` and `CURLSHOPT_SHARE(3)` man pages now also say that the limits apply to a shared connection cache.

---

Fixes #22265

@@ -79,6 +79,11 @@ in different threads using a shared connection.
 Note that when you use the multi interface, all easy handles added to the same
 multi handle share the connection cache by default without using this option.
 
+Connection limits set with CURLMOPT_MAX_HOST_CONNECTIONS(3) and
+CURLMOPT_MAX_TOTAL_CONNECTIONS(3) also apply to transfers using a shared
+connection cache. Each transfer applies the limits of the multi handle it
+runs on to the shared cache.
+
 ## CURL_LOCK_DATA_PSL
 
 The Public Suffix List stored in the share object is made available to all
